record.original_question: Consider selecting $r = O(k)$ uniformly random row indices $I$ and then choosing column indices $~J$ so that $A(I,:) A(I,~J) ~T$. What are sufficient conditions on $r$ and on the kernel $f$ which guarantee that | _~J A - A |_F <= c(n, m, k) | _J A - A |_F with high probability, where $c(n, m, k)$ grows at most logarithmically in its arguments? In other words, when does column selection on a random subset of the rows perform similarly to column selection on the full matrix?

evidence.quote: Consider selecting $r = \mathcal{O}(k)$ uniformly random row indices $I$ and then choosing column indices $\tilde{J}$ so that $A(I,:) \approx A(I,\tilde{J}) \tilde{T}$. What are sufficient conditions on $r$ and on the kernel $f$ which guarantee that \begin{equation} \|\Pi_{\tilde{J}} A - A\|_F \leq c(n, m, k) \|\Pi_J A - A\|_F \end{equation} with high probability, where $c(n, m, k)$ grows at most logarithmically in its arguments? In other words, when does column selection on a random subset of the rows perform similarly to column selection on the full matrix?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X = \{x_1,\dots,x_m\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and $Y = \{y_1,\dots,y_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, and let $f : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be a (symmetric, positive semidefinite) kernel. Form the kernel matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ with entries $A_{ij} = f(x_i, y_j)$. For any index set $J \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}$, write $A(:,J)$ for the submatrix of $A$ with columns indexed by $J$, and let $\Pi_J A := A(:,J) A(:,J)^{+} A$ denote the orthogonal projection of the columns of $A$ onto the column span of $A(:,J)$. Fix a target rank $k$ and let $J^\star$ denote a (near-)optimal column index set of size $k$ minimizing $\|\Pi_J A - A\|_F$ over all $|J| = k$.

Now consider the following two-stage random subsampling procedure:
1. Sample $r = \mathcal{O}(k)$ row indices $I \subseteq \{1,\dots,m\}$ uniformly at random (with or without replacement).
2. Choose column indices $\widetilde{J}$ of size $k$ together with a coefficient matrix $\widetilde{T}$ such that $A(I,:) \approx A(I,\widetilde{J})\,\widetilde{T}$ (i.e., perform column subset selection on the sub-row matrix $A(I,:)$ rather than on $A$).

Determine sufficient conditions on the sample size $r$ and on the kernel $f$ which guarantee that, with high probability,
$$\|\Pi_{\widetilde{J}} A - A\|_F \;\le\; c(n,m,k)\, \|\Pi_{J^\star} A - A\|_F,$$
where $c(n,m,k)$ grows at most polylogarithmically in $n$, $m$, and $k$. In other words, characterize the regimes (in $r$ and in properties of $f$) in which column selection performed on a uniformly random subset of the rows is as accurate, up to polylogarithmic factors, as column selection on the full kernel matrix.
artifact.category_tag: randomized column subset selection for kernel matrices
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on column and row subset selection (e.g., Cortinovis–Kressner 2020, and follow-ups through 2024–2025 on sublinear-time and randomized-embedding-based CSSP) provides partial results: sublinear-time algorithms based on uniformly random row sampling followed by strong RRQR refinement give approximation factors with polylogarithmic dependence in certain regimes, but a general characterization of sufficient conditions on the sample size $r$ and on the kernel $f$ that yields a polylogarithmic factor $c(n,m,k)$ for kernel matrices does not appear to have been completely established. The problem appears to remain open in the general kernel setting.

status_evidence.title: A sublinear-time randomized algorithm for column and row subset selection based on strong rank-revealing QR factorizations
status_evidence.snippet: An algorithm based on initial uniformly random selection of rows and columns, followed by refinement using strong RRQR; with random initial columns more steps are needed than with greedy selection.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial results on sublinear-time CSSP via random row sampling + RRQR refinement, but does not fully resolve the kernel-specific question.

status_evidence.title: Low-rank approximation in the Frobenius norm by column and row subset selection
status_evidence.snippet: Numerically robust variant of CSSP guaranteeing error close to best approximation in Frobenius norm.
status_evidence.claim: Provides foundational guarantees for combined column/row subset selection, motivating but not closing the kernel-specific question.
